source.title: Safety Layers in Aligned Large Language Models: The Key to LLM Security
source.authors: Shen Li; Liu-Yi Yao; Lan Zhang; Yaliang Li

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes aligned chat models on benign and mixed harmful/benign data and measures harmful response rates, directly testing the fine-tuning effects in V1 and V2. It also freezes or scales model layers and measures safety-related behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, compliant-token prefilling, suffix attacks, decoding changes, or whether safety training is concentrated at response openings. Its cited discussion of other work is not recorded as findings. Table 1 reports layer-scaling results using over-rejection as a proxy; Table 2 reports harmful rates after benign-data fine-tuning; Table 3 reports harmful rates after mixed harmful-data fine-tuning.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes four aligned chat models on benign, implicit, backdoor and mixed-harmful data. It measures harmful rate on AdvBench with Qi et al.'s GPT-4 judge template, which tests V1 and V2 with the original method. Freezing a located band of contiguous middle layers, plus an ablation freezing other layers, tests V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that a small contiguous band of middle layers ('safety layers'), created by alignment and absent in base models, distinguishes malicious from normal queries. Freezing these layers (SPPFT) largely prevents safety loss from benign, backdoor, mixed-harmful and reverse-DPO fine-tuning while keeping task performance. Freezing Wei et al.'s discrete neurons or other contiguous layers does not help.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses fine-tuning on normal, implicit, backdoor, and mixed harmful datasets and measures harmful rates, but it also introduces layer-freezing defenses and its own dataset and evaluation setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with the fine-tuning dataset, malicious-data proportion p, model, and whether safety-layer parameters are frozen. The layer-localization sweep also varies the scaled interval and scaling factor.

fits_no_version.finding: The last-token cosine similarity of normal vs malicious prompts diverges from normal-normal pairs starting in middle layers of aligned models. Pretrained bases show no gap (Figs 2, 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Aligned models separate harmful from benign prompts in a band of middle layers, a separation absent in base models.

fits_no_version.finding: Transplanting Llama-3-8B-Instruct's layers 16–31 into the base model improves answer quality but yields no refusals (A.5.3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal capability does not reside in the late layers of aligned models.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported harmful rates. The fine-tuning comparisons use study-specific datasets; the harmful-data tests mix malicious and normal examples rather than testing harmful-only data. Over-rejection is used as a proxy for locating safety layers.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was reached. Left out Table 1's other reported layer-range/scaling-factor combinations (Table 1); the selected rows retain three reported range outcomes per model. Table 3's Lisa results were omitted because the FullFT and SPPFT comparisons were prioritized. No Table 2 metrics other than harmful rate were extracted.

untested.parts: Harmful-only fine-tuning; fewer than 50 harmful examples; models beyond Llama-2-7b-chat and Phi-3-mini; learning rate fixed at 1e-5.
Benign datasets other than alpaca-finance-derived slices (alpaca-clean reported only for SPPFT); identity-shifting or other crafted benign data; LoRA/PEFT.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Ranks and individual weights. Localization is at layer level and spans 5–9 contiguous layers of 18–32. Whether so large a fraction counts as a 'small set' is untested.
Not tested. The aligned-vs-pretrained representation contrast shows that alignment creates the layers, not why safety is shallow.
No training that deepens safety beyond the first tokens.

missing.what: Ablation: freezing contiguous non-safety layers fails to protect. For example, Llama-3 DI with [0,5] frozen gives 65.77% and with [13,31] frozen 33.65%, versus SPPFT 6.15%.
Reverse DPO raises Rh to 26.5% (Llama-2), 41.6% (Llama-3), 31.3% (Phi-3) and 40.7% (gemma). Freezing the safety layers lowers these to 12.1/10.8/13.7/16.4%.
Scaling Llama-3 layers 7–12 by 1.2 cuts the number of AdvBench queries answered from 29 to 9. This is a direct harmful-compliance measure of the layer effect.
GPT-4 harmful scores (Sh) accompany every Rh value but were not extracted.

record.verdict_notes: The study is an ICLR 2025 paper and not an original source. The SPPFT rows are the study's own defense, so they were moved off V1/V2 and onto V5. The Table 1 over-rejection rows are boundary-selection values on benign prompts and were unlinked. The NFFT rows fail to protect, which bears on Wei et al.'s neuron-level localization; they stay on V2 only because a row has one state. The 'safety layers' cover 6–9 layers of 32 for the Llama models, so V5's 'small set' holds only loosely. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Tests mixed harmful-data fine-tuning at the stated data proportions; does not test fine-tuning on harmful examples alone or the full range of a few to a few hundred examples.
Tests normal, implicit, and backdoor fine-tuning datasets used in this study; does not test all forms of ordinary or carefully chosen benign data.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement across response positions.
No test of compliant-start prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
Tests contiguous layer ranges and freezing those layers; does not test ranks or identify a small set of individual weights.
Does not test whether training data or objective causes safety shallowness.
Does not test training designed to spread safety beyond initial response tokens.

labels.reason: The condition group mixes strong protection with incomplete protection. Tables 3 and 7 give 25.6% and 23.3% at p=0.1 (R40, R46), outside the stated near-baseline range. Retain supports for benign fine-tuning and p=0.05; assign limits_scope to p=0.1. Table 8 supports layer specificity.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Harmful fine-tuning at p=0.2 with safety layers frozen
labels.reason: Tables 3 and 7 show harmful rates of 68.3% and 78.8% despite frozen safety layers (R42, R48), qualifying the protection afforded by preserving those layers.

relation.reason: Its own fine-tuning results test safety erosion, and targeted layer interventions with other-layer controls test the concentration of safety-related effects.

tranche.reason: The study repeats harmful and benign fine-tuning with harmful-rate measurement on aligned models, and uses Qi et al.'s GPT-4 evaluation template for harmful scores.

source_check.notes:
The interventions establish concentration at the level of contiguous layer bands, without establishing individual-weight sparsity or an exclusive safety-carrying set.
Protection is already incomplete at p=0.1, before the larger failures at p=0.2.

reader_labels.reason: Freezing the identified safety layers limits the harmful-rate increase relative to FullFT, but rates still rise above baseline in every listed condition (R02, R05, R08, R11, R14, R17, R20, R23, R26, R29, R32, R35).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Layer scaling and fine-tuning with safety-layer parameters frozen, across tested models
reader_labels.reason: Layer-range scaling changes the reported over-rejection proxy, and SPPFT generally yields much lower harmful rates than full fine-tuning (R49–R60; R02, R05, R08, R11, R14, R17, R20, R23, R26, R29, R32, R35).

reader_labels.condition: Safety-layer freezing under higher harmful-data proportions and comparison with neuron freezing
reader_labels.reason: SPPFT does not prevent all degradation, particularly at p = 0.2; neuron freezing does not preserve safety in the benign-data experiments (R38–R48; R03, R06, R09, R12, R15, R18, R21, R24, R27, R30, R33, R36).
